items.title: Xi Poised to Press Trump on Arms Sales to Taiwan
items.summary: Beijing has called Taiwan the “core of China’s core interests.” Xi Jinping is likely to focus on getting President Trump to slow approval of more weapons for the self-governing island.

items.title: Chinese A.I. Firms Push Beyond Nvidia as DeepSeek Turns to Huawei
items.summary: Before this week’s U.S.-Chinese summit, Beijing reached a milestone in its quest for technological self-sufficiency.

items.title: China Increasingly Views Trump’s America as an Empire in Decline
items.summary: For decades, many Chinese viewed the United States with a mix of admiration, envy and resentment. President Trump’s volatile second term shattered that image.

items.title: RFK Jr. Is Driving a Vast Inquiry Into Vaccines, Despite His Public Silence
items.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has toned down his public criticism of vaccines, under orders from the White House. But inside his department, a sprawling research effort is a top priority.

items.title: Supreme Court Clears Path for Alabama to Use New Voting Map
items.summary: A majority of the justices sided with Alabama in a move that could speed up efforts to put in place a congressional district map that would eliminate a majority-Black district.

items.title: The Voting Rights Decision Might Silence Black People in Fayette County, Tennessee
items.summary: Black residents, who make up 25 percent of Fayette County, Tenn., won a new electoral map last year to change an all-white board of commissioners. They worry the Supreme Court’s ruling could threaten that.

items.title: Virginia Officials Ask Supreme Court to Restore Voting Map Drawn by Democrats
items.summary: State officials asked the justices to overturn a Virginia Supreme Court decision that struck down a congressional map, a major defeat for Democrats.

items.title: Why Republicans Are Still Drawing House Maps, While Democrats Are Stuck
items.summary: The G.O.P. has seized an edge on redistricting thanks to two court rulings, and it has more room to maneuver for extra seats before the midterms.

items.title: Starmer Faces Mounting Calls From Own Party to Resign as British Prime Minister
items.summary: Dozens of Labour Party leaders called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to leave office, and several government aides announced their resignations.

items.title: Justice Dept. Subpoenas Wall Street Journal in Leak Investigation
items.summary: Critics raised concerns over press freedom after The Journal disclosed receiving subpoenas related to an article on deliberations on the risks of military action in Iran.

items.title: Reflecting Pool Repairs to Cost $13.1 Million. Trump Had Promised $1.8 Million.
items.summary: The Interior Department added $6.2 million to the no-bid contract for repairs to the Lincoln Memorial pool late last week.

items.title: Kari Lake, Who Led Effort to Shutter Voice of America, Is Named Ambassador to Jamaica
items.summary: Ms. Lake tried and failed to fire hundreds of Voice of America journalists and to cut funding for other federally funded news groups like Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.

items.title: Nations Brace for Long-Term Economic Woes as Trump Calls Iran Truce Plan ‘Garbage’
items.summary: President Trump said the fragile cease-fire was on “life support,” and India’s leader urged residents to cut back on purchases and travel.

items.title: Trump Proposes Suspending Federal Gas Tax Until Prices Fall
items.summary: Congress would have to agree to any suspension, and dropping federal taxes would not make up for the steep increase in prices since the war began.

items.title: Is France’s Centrist Leader Trying to Weatherproof It From the Far Right?
items.summary: President Emmanuel Macron has appointed a string of allies who will remain in critical state positions after next year’s presidential election, and who could thwart a far-right successor.
